goals.text: 验证：神经网络的泛化行为能否作为 bootstrap 解空间刚性的探针

unknowns.text: The assumption that neural network generalization behavior directly reflects bootstrap solution space rigidity may oversimplify the relationship between model performance and theoretical stability metrics; this mapping lacks rigorous mathematical grounding in current literature.

Bootstrap resampling procedures used to estimate solution space variability may be computationally infeasible or statistically unstable when applied to high-dimensional neural network parameter spaces without proper regularization or dimensionality reduction.
There is no established benchmark dataset or ground-truth metric for “solution space rigidity” in neural networks, making validation of the proposed probe mechanism inherently circular or subjective.

The analysis may fail to account for architectural differences (e.g., CNNs vs. transformers) or training dynamics (e.g., learning rate schedules, optimizer choices) that independently affect both generalization and bootstrap-derived uncertainty estimates.

The physical analogy from condensed matter physics (e.g., phase transitions, electronic structure) used to motivate the concept of “rigidity” may not translate meaningfully to abstract function spaces in machine learning, risking misapplication of domain-specific concepts.
